transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, thanks for seeing me. What really brought me in is... well, my wife has been getting pretty frustrated with me lately. She'll be telling me about something important, like my cousin's appointments or who's giving him rides, and I'm looking right at her, listening... but then a minute later I realize I didn't actually take in half of what she said. It just sort of goes in one ear and out the other, even when I'm trying to pay attention.
Has this trouble focusing and remembering what people tell you been a problem for you since childhood, or is this something new that's developed recently?

No, it's definitely not a new thing. It's been going on since I was a kid. Even way back in grade school, well before I was 12, I remember my teachers telling my parents that I was a bright kid, but... I was just always daydreaming. I'd leave my completed homework sitting right inside my desk, and they constantly had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So, yeah, it's pretty much been a lifelong thing for me.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I haven't been feeling down or sad at all. I mean, I get a little annoyed with myself sometimes when I forget things, but... no, I still enjoy doing my usual stuff. My mood is generally pretty good.
